utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case number IT-02-60/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nikolic, are you able to follow the proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's a minor technical problem. Could you repeat your answer. Are you able to follow the proceedings? Are you receiving the interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm able to follow the proceedings. I'm able to follow the proceedings in a language that I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down. Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Mathias Marcussen, and today with me in Court is Ms. Susan Grogan, our case manager. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Marcussen. And could we have the appearances for the Defence, for Mr. Nikolic's defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour. On behalf of Mr. Nikolic, my name is Veselin Londrovic, lead counsel, and I'm assisted by my co-counsel, Lindsay Virginia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. With regard to the purpose of this Status Conference, pursuant to Rule 65 bis (i) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence that govern the Tribunal, a Status Conference must be held 120 days following the filing of the notice of appeal, and then every 120 days, to give the person who is appealing the possibility of raising issues that pertain thereto. In this case, a notice of appeal was filed by Mr. Nikolic on the 30th of December, 2003. This is, therefore, the first Status Conference held within the framework of the appeal. The purpose of the Status Conference is to allow the appellant to raise issues that concern the conditions in the detention facility or that concern his mental and physical health. Mr. Nikolic, or defence counsel for Mr. Nikolic, is there anything you would like to inform the Trial Chamber with regard to these matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have visited Mr. Nikolic. I did so on the 5th of April. We discussed his health condition and the conditions in the Detention Unit. As far as I am aware, Mr. Nikolic's health is quite good. He doesn't have any important or significant problems, as far as his health is concerned. As far as the personnel in the Detention Unit is concerned, they're treating Mr. Nikolic well, and as far as Mr. Nikolic's attitude in relation with the personnel in the Detention Unit is concerned, everything is fine, as far as I know. If Mr. Nikolic has anything else to add, he could address the Court himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Londrovic. Mr. Nikolic, is there anything you would like to add to what Defence counsel has just stated?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Microphone for the accused, please. His microphone is not switched on.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, there is nothing in particular that I would like to add as far as the conditions in the Detention Unit are concerned. The conditions are what they are. I have respect for those conditions and I have no objections to the way in which the personnel of the Detention Unit treats me. And similarly, I hope that the staff in the Detention Unit don't have any objections to raise with regard to my behaviour in the Detention Unit. All I can add is that after the sentence was handed down, I went through hell. That's how it is put colloquially in my country. To a large extent, I was mostly helped by the doctors who work in the Detention Unit, by the governor and his deputies, by the personnel who work in the Detention Unit. Naturally, I don't feel that good at the moment. My condition is not optimal. I think I need some time to return to the state I was in before the sentence was handed down, or to try to return to that state. I could also add that, if it's of any importance, for a long time after the sentence was handed down, I was quite simply not capable of getting involved in the case, to the extent that it is necessary to do so in order to help my Defence counsel to work on the appeal. So I think that this is the state I was in initially. I wasn't able to do anything or prepare for anything in a rational way in order to assist the preparation of my appeal. Naturally, the situation is different now. It's not as good as it could be or should be. All I can say is that I'm no longer able to cooperate, to work with my Defence counsel in a normal and rational way, and in view of this fact, I'm not in a position to assist them as I ought to be able to do. I hope you will understand what I'm saying. As far as extending the deadline is concerned, I hope that you will help me in that respect, and I hope that you will help me to assist my Defence counsel as much as possible, to enable them to file an appeal, to work on appeal that will be up to the necessary standards.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Nikolic. You may sit down now.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you for what you have said. I have taken note of the concerns you have expressed. Apart from those concerns, I would like to remind you that pursuant to Rule 44 and 48, that relate to the detention facilities, you can at any point in time file a complaint with the warden or with the registrar. Having said that, I would like to inform you of some of your obligations. The purpose of the Status Conference is to inform the appellant of the status of the proceedings with regard to this subject. The registry has informed the Trial Chamber that a version of the judgement in B/C/S was provided to you on the 1st of April. I would like to remind you, Mr. Nikolic, that filing of your Appeal Brief is expected for the 11th of May, 2004, at the latest. That is 40 days after the date on which you were provided with a B/C/S version of the judgement. The date will then be the 11th of May, unless, as you have just requested, your request to have the deadline extended, is granted. As there are no written submissions from either of the parties, I have no other issues to raise. I have no other questions for the parties at this point in time. Nevertheless, I would like to ask whether either of the parties has any comments to make or any issues that they would like to raise. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There's nothing on the part of the Prosecution. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Marcussen. Mr. Londrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at this moment, the Defence has nothing else to say. I see that you have been informed about our request for the extension of our appeal by the additional 14 days. In our request, we have stated the reasons for which we are asking for this extension, and we believe that your decision, when it's rendered, will be rendered as soon as possible, because we need to know whether the deadline is the 11th of May or whether we are going to be given the additional 14 days to prepare the appeal for Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Londrovic. I have taken note of what you have said, and since there are no other issues to be raised and considered, I would like -- I am adjourning this Status Conference. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. Maybe just in an effort to expedite the proceedings in this case, I'd like to mention that yesterday the Prosecution met with counsel for Mr. Nikolic, and was put on notice of the request for an extension of time. The Prosecution has not yet received the written motion, but I believe it's indicated in the motion that the Prosecution has no objection to the extension of 14 days in the sense that we will not be prejudiced by those 14 days. So maybe instead of us filing a written response, in the spirit of speeding up things, my stating this on the record could be taken as a response to the motion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Marcussen. What you have just said will be taken into consideration. This is going to assist us with rendering our decision. Is there anything else any of the parties would like to say? If not, we can adjourn. It is so decided.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
